title: Contextual Latency Canvas + Token Flow UI guidelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a compact, contextual per-model / per-route performance canvas that surfaces latency distributions, throughput, and token-level attribution in a developer-oriented layout. The canvas should make it easy to: (1) correlate p50/p95/p99 changes with recent rollouts, model variants and KV cache behavior, (2) inspect token waterfalls for high-cost requests, (3) explore throughput as both request-rate and tokens/second, and (4) toggle cost overlays for per-token cost attribution. Deliverables: Figma prototype with interactive states, a lightweight chart-spec doc for Engineering, and annotated handoff notes for product and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Figma prototype with desktop + narrow-panel responsive states and interactive time-window selector.
2) Chart-spec JSON (flat) describing each widget (latency bands, token waterfall, heatmap, microtrace swimlane) with data shape examples.
3) Design handoff annotated with expected sampling strategy and fallback when token-level telemetry is missing.
4) PM and Eng review signoff recorded; feedback items converted to follow-ups.
5) Accessibility contrast checks passed for color scales and hover targets.
design_notes:
- Default primary metric: p95 latency for the selected time window; show p50/p75/p95/p99 as overlaid ribbons.
- Use 'contextual panes' to reduce cognitive load: header (summary metrics), latency canvas (ribbon + violin), token inspector (waterfall + top tokens list), throughput lane (heatmap + rps sparkline), and rollout strip (model variant timeline).
- Introduce KV cache-hit overlay: toggle to shade latency ribbon where prefix cache hit ratio > 40%.
- Token waterfall: show relative cost per token, source (user vs system), and whether token came from cached KV. Provide collapse/expand for long sequences.
- Sampling tradeoff: default to full-precision for the last 15 minutes, 1:10 sampling for 1-24 hours, pre-aggregated histograms for >24 hours. Documented in handoff.
- Interaction patterns: hover across the ribbon should show linked highlights in waterfall and throughput lanes; clicking a microtrace opens the Request Inspector panel (linked to an existing PRD).
- Color: use single-hue diverging palette for latency bands (low -> high) and a separate hue for cost overlays to avoid misinterpretation.
chart_specs:
LATENCY_CANVAS: layered area + median line + percentile ribbons; x-axis = time (ms resolution), y-axis = latency ms; series = {p50,p75,p95,p99}; show quantile shading, tooltip lists quantiles and sample count.
THROUGHPUT_HEATMAP: x-axis = time, y-axis = token-length buckets (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024); cell color = tokens/sec; allow logarithmic color scale toggle.
TOKEN_WATERFALL: horizontal swimlane per-token with bars scaled by token-cost; metadata badges for 'cache-hit', 'external-tool' or 'function-call'; ability to collapse by token-type.
MICROTRACE_SWIMLANE: discrete lanes for model-variant, region, and capacity-tier; show vertical markers for rollouts and incidents.
COST_OVERLAY: optional line overlay on latency canvas; units = $/1000 tokens; min-max axis auto-scales with clear legend.
SUNBURST_PREFIX_MATCH: when a route is selected, show a sunburst of frequent prefix patterns causing highest latency or cost.
DEFAULT_TIME_WINDOWS: [15m,1h,6h,24h,7d]; default = 15m with live streaming enabled.
DATA_EXAMPLES: include flattened arrays for histogram buckets and token arrays in handoff spec.
decisions:
- Primary latency summary will be p95 (product + SRE alignment).
- Token-level telemetry remains opt-in per workspace due to storage cost; UI will show a prominent 'Token telemetry disabled' state with a CTA to enable.
- Chosen default color scale: Blues (low) -> Reds (high) for latency; Greens for cost overlay to avoid red/blue confusion in color-blind palettes.
- Time-window default set to 15m in desktop to emphasize live behavior; allow manual persistence across sessions.
- We will not show raw request payloads in the public console by default; Request Inspector will respect masking and redaction policy.

notes_for_engineering: Provide flattened histogram buckets and an optional token array payload. If token telemetry is disabled, return a 'telemetry_disabled' flag; UI should show CTA. Sampling rules: last 15m full fidelity, 1:10 for 1-24h, histograms beyond. Keep endpoint paginated for long token sequences.
qa_criteria: Widget render across time windows with synthetic data; hover linking highlights between canvases; correct annotation of rollout markers; rendering fallback when token telemetry is disabled; color contrast checks (AA).
notes: This ticket focuses purely on the design and chart-spec deliverables. Implementation work will be split into separate ENG tickets for telemetry, UI components and rollout annotations.
